headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Cline’s workspace/file access and broad egress can collide with kotaemon’s document/API-key handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads workspace files and uses MCP, so it can ingest content that kotaemon may generate or store in ./ktem_app_data. Kotaemon is a web-UI RAG system that processes documents and chat transcripts, making prompt-like content plausible. The bridge is indirect, but shared file-based interaction makes instruction hijacking feasible.
conditions: IF Cline reads kotaemon-produced files from the shared workspace or ./ktem_app_data, injected instructions can reach its tool loop.
IF kotaemon renders attacker-controlled document text into outputs that Cline later treats as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable MCP servers for Cline during cross-agent runs.
Restrict kotaemon to read-only ingestion folders.
Add a manual review step before Cline acts on kotaemon output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem access and handles model-provider API keys; kotaemon stores data in ./ktem_app_data and handles API keys plus documents, PDFs, and chat transcripts. If they share a workspace or host, either agent can expose sensitive files, and Cline’s broad egress increases exfiltration risk. This is a default-dangerous pairwise leakage pathway.
conditions: IF both agents run on the same host with overlapping filesystem access, sensitive kotaemon data can be read by Cline.
IF Cline is allowed to send context to external model providers, any leaked file contents can leave the environment.
mitigations: Place kotaemon data on a separate volume.
Remove shared workspace access for Cline.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Constrain Cline egress with a firewall or proxy.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; kotaemon writes ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so concurrent writes can collide on shared files or state. The overlap is real, though not as broad as unrestricted shared git mutation.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace or data directory, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Cline operates on a git repo that kotaemon also touches, git state corruption or conflicting commits can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Back up shared files before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce code, browser-derived artifacts, and filesystem changes; kotaemon ingests documents and citations for downstream chat/RAG outputs. If kotaemon consumes Cline-generated content without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect answers or actions. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary, so the default risk is moderate.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses Cline-generated files or notes as source documents, its answers can inherit Cline’s mistakes.
IF Cline relies on kotaemon outputs as authoritative without human review, downstream actions may amplify errors.
mitigations: Require human review of Cline outputs before ingestion.
Mark kotaemon sources from Cline as untrusted.
Add citation checks before publishing answers.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source corpora.
requires-engineering: implement verification and provenance scoring.

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and diverse document classes, while Cline handles model-provider keys and workspace files. If regulated or sensitive documents are placed into kotaemon and then exposed through Cline’s broader workspace access or external model calls, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are stored in kotaemon and accessible to Cline, compliance scope expands.
IF either agent forwards those materials to a third-party model provider, retention and residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into either agent.
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Review provider retention settings for both agents.
Rotate any keys used in test runs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
